results.comment: "If everything is of equal importance, then you're paralyzed".   1:02:52 mark.    Insightful comment by Dr. Peterson.  This can even happen in large military organizations.  When I was still on active duty, USSOCOM was infamous for making everything top priority.  CENTCOM, EUCOM, PACOM, SOUTHCOM - all of it was top priority.  And inside each of those geographical regions, such as CENTCOM ie the Middle East, we at the lower HQ level (I was an Air Force special operations planner at the time) would ask, which nations were the most important to focus on?  The answer, more or less, was to focus on all of them.   I think it was driven by a desire to keep a lid on the overall situation by dealing with threats as they emerged (this was in 2008-2009, by the way), but it made it really hard to do any long- or even medium-term planning.
